description: Games getting the most TikTok views right now (Roblox, Steam): TikTok views of videos PUBLISHED in the last 7 or 30 days (by publish date, not views gained), with 2+ distinct creators, crossed with players online and 24 h growth. Badges: hype_over_players (attention ahead of players), viral_and_growing (top views and players rising, never a game in decline), new_and_viral (14 days old or less). state=warming_up means coverage is still thin. network=youtube lists YouTube videos one by one with their own view count (never summed or ranked per game). Unreleased games are rare. Only games Wieldr already tracks are probed for videos. Every game carries asOf (export time, UTC), source and grade (grade = completeness of the game record (A = 8+ of 10 data points known, B = 6-7, C = 4-5, D = fewer); estimate grade: B = tighter range, C = wide range, D = very rough order of magnitude.) Revenue figures are estimates with a range and a grade, never measured sales and never a guarantee. Definitions: resource wieldr://methodology.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous call, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

limit.description: How many results per page (default 10, max 25).

maxPlayers.description: Maximum players online now (small games getting attention).

minCreators.description: Minimum distinct TikTok creators in the window (default 2).

network.description: tiktok (default: ranked games) or youtube (list of videos with their raw view counts).

niche.description: Niche label, key or keyword: a ranked Roblox or Fortnite niche (e.g. "Ragdoll", "Tycoon", from list_niches), a genre (e.g. "Simulation") or a word in game titles (e.g. "brainrot").

platform.description: roblox or steam (the platforms probed for videos). Omit for both.

sort.description: views (default), viewsPerDay (average daily views since publication) or creators.

status.description: released, early_access (Steam) or unreleased (rare). Omit for all.

window.description: Publish window of the videos: 7d (default) or 30d.

method.description: One useful sentence; full definitions in the MCP resource wieldr://methodology.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as cursor for the next page; null = last page.
